passages.original: Haec ideo ingressi, ne quis aliter mentiatur, et æstimet credendum mendaciis Judaeorum. De quo ipsi perfidi testantur, dicente Josepho historiarum scriptore, quod fuerit illo tempore vir sapiens (sl tamen oportet, inquit, virum dici), mirabilium crea- torem operum, qui apparuit discipulis suis, post triduum mortis suae vivens secundum prophetarum scripta : qui et haec et alia innumerabilia de eo plena miraculis prophetaverunt : ex quo coepit congregatio Christianorum , et in on.ne hominum penetravit genus : nec ulla natio Romani orbis remansit, quæ cultus ejas expers relinqueretur.
passages.english: We have entered upon these matters for this reason: so that no one may lie otherwise, and suppose that the lies of the Jews are to be believed. Concerning him the faithless themselves bear witness, since Josephus, the writer of histories, says that there was at that time a wise man (if indeed, he says, it is right to call him a man), a worker of wonderful deeds, who appeared to his disciples alive three days after his death, according to the writings of the prophets, who prophesied both these things and countless other things full of miracles about him; from him began the community of Christians, and it penetrated into every race of men, nor did any nation of the Roman world remain that was left without a share in his worship.
passages.notes: Scanning errors silently corrected: 'sl' for 'si', 'crea- torem' for 'creatorem', 'on.ne' for 'omne', 'ejas' for 'ejus'. The passage paraphrases Josephus's testimony about Jesus (the 'Testimonium Flavianum').
